_what: The general maximum-drift-rate guideline the abstract and conclusion 8 compare our ceiling against. Frozen here so the build makes no network call and so the number is never typed into a generator or into LaTeX.
reference: Sheikh S. Z., Wright J. T., Siemion A. P. V., Enriquez J. E., 2019, ApJ, 884, 14
quotation: We determine that a normalized drift rate of 200 nHz (e.g., 200 Hz s^-1 at 1 GHz) is a generous, physically motivated guideline for the maximum drift rate that should be applied to future narrowband SETI projects if computational capabilities permit.
source_of_quotation: abstract of the published paper (ADS 2019ApJ...884...14S), read 2026-10-08
_two_sided_note: The recommendation is plus-or-minus 200 nHz, i.e. a full range of 400 nHz about zero. Our own ceiling macros \DriftCeilLo and \DriftCeilHi are likewise one-sided half-widths read off each window's own +-drift_max, so the ratio below compares like with like: one-sided half-width against one-sided half-width.
_jupiter_note: Quoted by the reviewer as the acceleration of a transmitter on Jupiter's equator from the planet's rotation alone; recomputed here from omega^2 R_eq with R_eq = 71492 km and P = 9.925 h, which gives 2.21 m s^-2, so the figure is reproduced rather than taken on trust.
